## Intent

The bug reproduces on a test network and not on the deployment that pays. Testnet-only findings are filed at Critical because the testnet PoC is convincing, and rejected because the deployed code differs.

## Detection signals

Signals say the reproduction was testnet-only, or that mainnet is unaffected or behaves differently.

Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched against the full text of the
draft finding, subject to the engine rules below.

**Fires when at least one of these matches:**

```text
  testnet[- ]only
  (only|just) (reproduced|demonstrated|verified) on (the )?testnet
  mainnet (is|deployment is) (unaffected|not at risk|different)
  not (derivable|present) on mainnet
```

## Escape hatches

None. Either the deployed configuration is affected or it is not.

## Known false-positive modes

These are the shapes where the rule fires on something it should not. They are the
reason a firing is a prompt to check, not a verdict.

- A finding verified on a mainnet fork, where the report says "testnet" to describe the RPC endpoint used.
- A finding about a contract that is genuinely deployed on a test network and pays under that program's rules.
- A report that states mainnet impact separately and is flagged on a passing mention of the testnet.

## Synthetic examples

Both examples are synthetic. They describe no real report and no real target.

**Fires:** "Reproduced on testnet only; mainnet is unaffected."

**Does not fire:** "Verified against the live mainnet deployment at the pinned block."

## Corrective action

Verify mainnet impact exists. If not, do not submit as Critical.
